errors.description: The frame is not valid JSON.
The frame is JSON but not a valid JSON-RPC 2.0 request (batches are not supported).
No handler is registered for the method.
The params do not match the method's schema.
An unexpected failure inside hx. Infrastructure failure, not a tool outcome.
A settings file or the plugin settings failed schema validation. data.errors lists file, key, expected and found for each problem.
The permission policy blocked a tool call. A policy decision is surfaced to the model as a tool error, and to RPC callers with this code.
The session's mode can no longer change: the first prompt has been submitted and the system prompt is frozen for prompt caching.
The session ledger failed verification. It is never repaired silently. `data.broken_at_seq` names the first bad event when known.
The ledger refused an event that contraprova's task projection does not allow. The event was not written.
The ledger could not be opened or written (I/O error, lock timeout).
The session reached its cost cap. New turns are blocked until the cap is raised.
The hx binary is missing, could not be started, or kept crashing and the plugin stopped restarting it. A client-side failure: hx itself never sends it.
An hx call did not answer within the plugin's per-call timeout. The plugin sent $/cancelRequest first; data.cancelled says whether hx answered it.
The price catalogue could not be fetched, or the cached models-dev.json is not a valid catalogue. The previous file is left as it was.
`prices.refresh` was called while the plugin's `prices.refresh_enabled` setting is false.
The request was cancelled with $/cancelRequest before it changed anything.
Too many requests are queued; retry later.
A request frame exceeded the maximum size and was dropped.
At least one edit failed validation. Nothing was written. data.failures lists each failed edit with the closest match and its line numbers.
An edit targets a path outside the allowed globs. Checked before journaling. data.paths lists the paths.
An edit targets a protected path. Checked before journaling. data.paths lists the paths.
The workspace root cannot be opened as a directory.
The transaction exceeds a size or count limit.
A touched file changed between validation and write. Nothing was written.
Another transaction holds the workspace lock.
A write failed after the transaction started. The workspace was restored from the journal; data.restored is true.
No journal with that id exists in the journal directory.
The journal's manifest or data failed verification. Nothing was changed.
The journal is in use by a live transaction.
The journal is not in a state that allows this operation.
Restoring from the journal failed. The journal is kept; run txn.recover or retry txn.restore.
An unexpected I/O failure before any workspace write.
A parameter is out of range or malformed: empty pattern, zero budget, bad line range, bad glob.
The search pattern does not compile as a regular expression.
root is not an existing directory.
A path is absolute, contains .., or resolves through a symlink outside root.
A named file or directory does not exist under root.
lang was given explicitly and no grammar is registered for it.
`tree-sitter` could not produce a tree (parser setup failure or internal timeout).
The `git` CLI is missing, exited with an error or printed output that could not be parsed.
The deadline passed before the call finished.
An embedded data file (`redact.rules.json`, `never_pack.json`, `languages.json`) or a query does not load. Fails closed.
An unexpected operating-system error while reading under root.
The platform cannot enforce a requested sandbox dimension and the policy did not allow degrading it. Nothing ran. data.dimension and data.reason say which.
The OS refused while the sandbox was being built or applied, so the command did not run. data.step names the setup step.
A long-lived sandboxed child could not be started (`sandbox.spawn` only; `sandbox.run` reports the same condition as the exit kind `spawn_failed`).
No running sandbox child has that handle: it never existed, or sandbox.wait already returned its exit.
Too many sandbox children are running at once; wait for or kill one.

Mods cannot run here: the sandboxed worker needs a private channel and an enforcing sandbox, and this platform has none (Windows today). Nothing ran, and mods never fall back to running unsandboxed. data.reason says why.
A mod could not be loaded: unreadable or invalid files, a failed import, a `register` that threw or ran past its budget. The message names the plugin and the cause.
The plugin's hooks/hooks.json has no `modules` key, so there is nothing to run.
A mod with this name is already loaded in the session; unload it first.
No mod worker runs for this session: load a mod first.
The sandboxed worker exited, crashed or stopped answering. Its mods are gone; load them again. data.stderr holds the last of its error output.
The worker's runtime could not be driven to an answer (a stalled chain). The session's mods must be reloaded.
hx has no connection to the plugin to ask about a `$` call (a one-shot run, not `hx serve`).
The plugin did not answer a `$` call in time; the mod's promise rejects with this code.
A `$` call could not reach the plugin, or the plugin failed while performing it.
A `$` call that boopis does not provide yet (process, mcp, model, agent, tool, prompt, turn, settings, audio, telemetry). It is refused by name, never ignored.
The exec kernel exited, was killed (hard timeout, an unresponsive cancel, its lifetime limit) or lost its channel. Its variables are gone; the next exec call starts a fresh kernel.
A cell made more tool calls than the per-cell limit (`exec.max_calls_per_cell`).
The kernel is running a cell, or too many kernels are busy to start another.
A harness feature is not available yet (diagnostics, waiting on a form). The answer says so instead of inventing one.
`harness.sh` could not start the command (the program was not found or could not be executed).
A harness call had malformed arguments, or exec was called without a session or working directory.
Hermes is not installed, cannot be started, or its gateway cannot be reached. The host's own code; the plugin never sends it.
The installed Hermes is older than `requires_hermes`, or its gateway speaks a protocol or code identity the host cannot use.
An action that needs the user's consent (running an installer, changing Hermes's configuration) was requested without `consent: true`. Nothing ran.
A request on the host's local channel carried a wrong or missing token. Nothing was read.
A gateway frame is not a valid JSON-RPC 2.0 message or is larger than the cap. It was not forwarded.
The connection id is not (or no longer) open.
A request from Hermes needed an answer and no window is attached to give it, so the host declined it.
The operating system refused or failed an integration call (dialog, notification, opener).

No secret store is available: on Linux, no Secret Service (GNOME Keyring or `KWallet` 6) is running or unlocked. The message names the fix. Also sent when a plugin asks the host for a secret and the host's channel is not there.
The secret store refused or failed an operation. No secret value is ever in the message.
No secret is stored under that service and account.
A secret reference is not `secret://<scope>/<name>`, or names a scope or name outside the allowed characters.
First-run setup found no usable Hermes. The step carries the documented install command; nothing was installed.
The app does not carry the plugin or the hx binary it should install (a development build, or a damaged bundle).
The plugin could not be copied into the profile's plugins directory, or Hermes did not enable it.
`hermes config set` refused or failed a change. data.key names the key; nothing after it was applied.
The user declined the Hermes configuration changes. Setup stops there and says what will not work.
An answer does not match the form that is open (a different form id, a value outside the schema, a missing field).
The setup progress file is unreadable or written by a newer version. It is kept as it was and setup starts again from the checks.
After setup, the plugin did not answer `describe` or reported a configuration problem. data.errors lists them.
A form's schema is not a flat MCP elicitation object with the supported field types. data.errors lists each problem.
The submitted values do not satisfy the form's schema. data.errors lists file, key, expected and found; secret values are never in them.
No form has that id (it never existed, or the plugin restarted).
The form is already submitted, cancelled or expired.
`wait=true` ran out of time before the form was answered. The form stays open and can still be answered.
A secret field was reported as provided but the host holds no secret at its reference.
The form asks for something not available yet (for example a picker the host does not serve, or wait=true inside a cell past its timeout).
Too many forms are open in this session; answer or cancel one first.
A connector with that name is already in Hermes. Nothing was changed.
Hermes has no connector (MCP server) with that name.
Hermes refused the connector's configuration (its own validation, such as a suspicious command). Nothing was kept.
What would be installed is not what the form showed (the collection or the request changed). Nothing was installed; review again.
A key the connector needs was not given. Nothing was installed.
The server comes from a Hermes plugin and cannot be changed here; change the plugin.
The server does not sign in with OAuth, so there is nothing to sign in to.
Hermes's OAuth flow failed; the message is Hermes's own reason. No token was stored.
The user cancelled the sign-in. Hermes closed its listener.
The browser did not finish the sign-in in time. The host cancelled the flow, which closes Hermes's loopback listener.
A provider's own login command could not be started (not installed, not on the PATH).
Hermes refused or failed a connector call; the message names the call and Hermes's reason. Never carries a key.
There is no teammate (Hermes profile) with that name.
A teammate with that name exists already (restoring an archived teammate whose name was taken again).
The teammates' RPC refused: the default profile is not a teammate, an archived teammate is read only, or a delete was not confirmed with the teammate's name.
Hermes's own `profile rename` or `profile delete` failed. data.output is what it said.
